correctness.rationale: The explicit graph-metric clique complexes on 16, 18, 20, 22, 24 vertices have face vectors (16,68,104,58,8), (18,81,117,63,9), (20,90,140,80,12), (22,99,143,77,11), (24,108,160,84,12). The complete acyclic Morse certificates have critical vectors (one 0-cell plus respectively 1 two-cell, 1 one-cell, 1 two-cell, 1 one-cell, 3 two-cells). All simplex incidences and whole Hasse diagram acyclicity are checked independently from the generated graph in the provided standalone verifier. Forman discrete Morse theory then yields exactly S², S¹, S², S¹, wedge of three S². No inference about integral homotopy is based on field homology alone. Critical nonstandard assertion (each displayed Morse matching is acyclic) is certified by the full matched-pair list and an independent topological sort of each complete oriented face-incidence graph. In dimensions at most two, one vertex and zero edges makes every two-cell attaching map constant; one vertex plus one edge and no higher cells forms a circle. The complete domain n∈{8,9,10,11,12} and inclusive shortest-path threshold two are explicit.

originality.rationale: The closest public generalized-Petersen result establishes a scale-two circle collapse only for n≥13 and at n=12 only three independent mod-two degree-two homology classes. Such a homology calculation alone cannot identify the fundamental group, torsion, or homotopy attaching maps; it does not imply a wedge of three integral two-spheres. The graph-square theorem of Adamaszek has a girth≥7 hypothesis at this radius, which these graphs fail. Full scale-two Boolean-level and hypercube results concern nonisomorphic metric spaces. Historical claims in an accessible prior research ledger were compared for the five values and equivalent homotopy forms; a published dodecahedral homology/symmetry study refers to a distinct invariant and does not imply the five-case classification. The literature comparisons support originality under the inspected evidence, with explicitly stated bibliographic risks.
residual_risks: Published and unindexed computations could contain a logically equivalent finite five-case homotopy classification.
Full text of the indexed generalized-Petersen boundary record was inaccessible at the time of inspection: its indexed summary was compared but cannot exclude an unreported full-text appendix.
The present finding does not imply any result outside n=8,...,12 at radius 2 or certify global publication priority.

value.rationale: Exactly n=8,...,12 is the naturally distinguished complete small-parameter interval directly below the n≥13 scale-two Rips collapse theorem, above the separately investigated n=7 case. This classifies an unstable transition rather than an arbitrary selected few numbers. The alternating S²/S¹ homotopy types and the final triple sphere wedge exhibit genuinely different topological regimes; n=12 upgrades a specifically known mod-two boundary observation to an integral simply connected homotopy classification. Exact full homotopy types and explicit finite acyclic Morse certificates are useful independently of a general n theorem.
